title: PublishHistory
description: The per-post table recommend-publish-timing computes from. PublishRequest carries only aggregate counts, which is enough to describe a cohort but not enough to bucket it, so the rows live here. v2 carries a panel of metrics per post rather than one: v1 kept a single figure and dropped likes and comments on the way in, which made it impossible to ask whether several metrics agree about a window — and agreement across metrics is what a creator can actually judge, where a p-value is not. Captions and post content stay out; timing needs when and how well, nothing else.

mode.description: How the rows were obtained. A provided export is still owner-authorised data; it is not public scraping.

timestamps.description: Whether a publishing hour can be recovered at all, and in which zone. An unconfirmed zone no longer stops the analysis — the windows are simply reported as UTC and the creator is asked once — but a source that reports no hour at all still does.

timezone.description: The offset every row carries, or 'mixed'.

rows_checked.description: How many catalogue rows the offset claim was measured on. Measured across the whole export, not only the rows that survive filtering, because the claim is about the export.

local_time_recoverable.description: Whether every exported row carries an absolute instant, i.e. a UTC offset. When it does, the creator's local hour is a conversion rather than a guess and needs only their zone, which the host supplies on the request. Three producers used to hard-code this false and the engine answered in UTC on every run; the information was present the whole time and was simply never converted. It no longer gates anything — an unresolvable zone identifier does.

time_of_day_recoverable.description: Whether the rows carry a real clock time at all. False when every timestamp is midnight, which is what a date-only or estimated source produces. This one still forces a refusal: there is no hour to rank in any zone.

date_precision.description: estimated_day means an upstream source inferred the calendar date rather than reporting a platform timestamp. Such rows must not be used for time-of-day ranking.

metric_panel.description: Every metric these rows carry, each declaring which direction is good and where it came from. Platforms get their own panel because their data is not the same: an Instagram owner export knows reach, saves and skip rate, while a public YouTube read knows views, likes and comments and nothing about the audience that skipped.

direction.description: Skip rate is the reason this field exists: ranking it the same way as views would put the worst window on top.

derived_from.description: Set for ratios such as like_rate. A rate divides out how far the platform distributed the post, so it tracks how the audience that did see it responded — which is the part a publish hour could plausibly move.

accumulates_with_age.description: True for lifetime counters. When true the recommendation must state the maturity confound: an older post carries more of the metric regardless of publish hour.

scope.description: owner metrics come from the account holder's own analytics; public counters come from the open API. A single ranking must never mix the two.

posts_carrying.description: How many rows actually have this metric. A metric present on three posts must not carry the same weight as one present on all of them.

owner_scope.description: Audit of account ownership before timing projection. Unattributed rows remain visible in the cohort but are not covered by the owner claim.

coverage.description: What was dropped on the way to the usable rows. A cohort that looks clean because the failures were filtered out is the failure mode this block exists to prevent.

cohort_total.description: Posts of the requested format, before the metric and maturity filters.

cohort_with_metric.description: Rows carrying at least one panel metric.

posts.description: One row per post. Only what a timing comparison consumes.

post_ref.description: Public shortcode or video id; enough to open the post, not enough to carry its content.

metrics.description: Keyed by metric_panel name. null means this post does not carry that metric — a partial export is normal and must not be read as a zero.
